description: Integrate Proton profiler into vLLM: backend, config, and contiguous profiling with periodic flushing

userStories.title: Add Proton config fields to ProfilerConfig
userStories.description: As a developer, I need Proton-specific fields in ProfilerConfig so users can configure Proton through --profiler-config JSON.
acceptanceCriteria: ProfilerConfig in vllm/config/profiler.py has field proton_profiler_dir: str (default '')
ProfilerConfig has field proton_context: str — 'shadow' or 'python' (default 'shadow')
ProfilerConfig has field proton_data: str — 'tree' or 'trace' (default 'tree')
ProfilerConfig has field proton_backend: str | None — 'cupti', 'roctracer', 'instrumentation', or None (default None)
ProfilerConfig has field proton_mode: str | None — free-form backend-specific string (default None)
ProfilerConfig has field proton_hook: str | None — 'triton' or None (default None)
All fields have docstrings explaining valid values
Existing torch/cuda config fields are unchanged
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Follow the torch_profiler_* naming pattern but with proton_ prefix. Refer to Proton CLI flags: -n/--name, -b/--backend, -c/--context, -m/--mode, -d/--data, -k/--hook. Proton source at submodules/triton/third_party/proton.

userStories.title: Add validation for Proton config fields
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the config to validate Proton fields so users get clear errors for invalid values.
acceptanceCriteria: When profiler='proton', proton_profiler_dir must be set (non-empty) — raises validation error otherwise
proton_context is validated to be 'shadow' or 'python'
proton_data is validated to be 'tree' or 'trace'
proton_backend is validated to be 'cupti', 'roctracer', 'instrumentation', or None
proton_hook is validated to be 'triton' or None
proton_mode accepts any string without validation (backend-dependent)
proton_profiler_dir is converted to absolute path (same URI scheme handling as torch_profiler_dir)
Validation errors produce clear messages indicating valid options
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Add validation in the existing @model_validator(mode='after') method. Follow the same pattern as torch_profiler_dir validation.

userStories.title: Wire Proton config into ProtonProfilerWrapper
userStories.description: As a developer, I need ProtonProfilerWrapper to read the new config fields and pass them to proton.start().
acceptanceCriteria: ProtonProfilerWrapper.__init__() reads all 6 Proton config fields from ProfilerConfig
_start() calls proton.start(name=..., context=..., data=..., backend=..., mode=..., hook=...)
Output file is written to proton_profiler_dir
Existing scheduling via delay_iterations, max_iterations, warmup_iterations, active_iterations, wait_iterations continues to work
Docstrings and inline comments explain each parameter mapping
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: ProtonProfilerWrapper already exists in vllm/profiler/wrapper.py. Update it to use the new config fields instead of hardcoded defaults. GPU worker profile() method in vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py may need updating to pass new config fields.

userStories.title: Write tests for Proton config validation and wiring
userStories.description: As a developer, I need tests that verify Proton config fields are validated and wired correctly.
acceptanceCriteria: Unit test: ProfilerConfig(profiler='proton', proton_profiler_dir='/tmp/proton') creates valid config
Unit test: ProfilerConfig(profiler='proton') without proton_profiler_dir raises validation error
Unit test: invalid proton_context value raises validation error
Unit test: invalid proton_data value raises validation error
Unit test: invalid proton_backend value raises validation error
Unit test: invalid proton_hook value raises validation error
Unit test: proton_mode accepts arbitrary strings without error
Integration test: Proton config fields are correctly passed to proton.start() arguments
All existing profiler config tests continue to pass
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Existing test file at tests/v1/worker/test_proton_profiler.py. Add config validation tests there or in a new test file.

userStories.title: End-to-end validation with proton config options
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to validate that Proton config options work end-to-end with vllm serve.
acceptanceCriteria: vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b --profiler-config '{"profiler": "proton", "proton_profiler_dir": "/tmp/proton_output", "proton_context": "shadow", "proton_data": "tree", "proton_hook": "triton"}' starts without errors
Triggering /start_profile and /stop_profile produces profiling output in /tmp/proton_output
Output format matches proton_data setting (tree produces .hatchet file, trace produces .chrome_trace file)
Changing proton_context to 'python' produces Python-context profiling data
userStories.notes: The openai/gpt-oss-20b model requires --tensor-parallel-size 2 on 2x L40S GPUs. Server startup takes ~80s. Use proton_profiler_dir instead of torch_profiler_dir for the output directory.

userStories.title: Support periodic_flushing mode in ProtonProfilerWrapper
userStories.description: As a developer, I need ProtonProfilerWrapper to support Proton's periodic_flushing mode so profiling data is automatically flushed to per-phase files during long-running sessions.
acceptanceCriteria: Detect 'periodic_flushing' prefix in proton_mode to switch to persistent session lifecycle
Session is created once on first _start() call and reused across subsequent start/stop cycles
_start() calls proton.activate(session) in periodic mode instead of proton.start()
_stop() calls proton.deactivate(session, flushing=True) in periodic mode instead of proton.finalize()
proton.finalize() is only called on shutdown(), not on every stop
Per-phase .part_N output files are written automatically by Proton during deactivate
Non-periodic mode continues to work as before (start/finalize per cycle)
Docstrings explain both periodic and non-periodic modes
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Check for 'periodic_flushing' prefix in proton_mode (it may be 'periodic_flushing' or 'periodic_flushing:format=hatchet_msgpack'). Store a _periodic_mode bool flag in __init__. Session created lazily on first _start(). Proton API: proton.activate(session), proton.deactivate(session, flushing=True), proton.finalize(session).

userStories.title: Add phase tracking to ProtonProfilerWrapper
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the wrapper to track phase state so the status endpoint can report profiling progress.
acceptanceCriteria: Wrapper tracks current phase number (starts at 0, increments on each stop cycle in periodic mode)
Wrapper tracks list of output file paths generated so far
Wrapper exposes a get_status() method returning dict with: active (bool), current_phase (int), output_dir (str), output_files (list of str)
Phase advances on each _stop() call in periodic mode via proton.data.advance_phase(session)
get_status() works for both periodic and non-periodic modes
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: proton.data.advance_phase(session) returns the new phase number. Output files follow pattern: <name>.part_N.<format>. Track files by scanning proton_profiler_dir or building the list from known phase numbers and format.

userStories.title: Add /profile_status API endpoint
userStories.description: As a user, I want to query profiling status to see the current phase, which files have been written, and whether profiling is active.
acceptanceCriteria: New GET /profile_status endpoint in vllm/entrypoints/serve/profile/api_router.py
Returns JSON with: active (bool), profiler (str), current_phase (int), output_dir (str), output_files (list of str)
Returns 200 with empty/default response when no profiler is configured
Endpoint is registered alongside existing /start_profile and /stop_profile
Status plumbed through engine/core to worker similar to start/stop profile API
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Look at how /start_profile and /stop_profile are implemented in api_router.py and trace the path through async_llm.py → EngineCore → Worker. The status query needs the same plumbing. Return type should be a simple dict/JSON response.

userStories.title: Wire periodic mode through GPU worker shutdown
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the GPU worker to call finalize() on shutdown in periodic mode to flush remaining data.
acceptanceCriteria: GPU worker's shutdown or cleanup path calls profiler.shutdown()
ProtonProfilerWrapper.shutdown() calls proton.finalize(session) in periodic mode to flush remaining phases
Multiple start/stop cycles before shutdown produce sequential .part_N files without errors
Works correctly with multi-rank (TP > 1) — each rank produces its own .part_N files
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The WorkerProfiler base class already has a shutdown() method that calls stop(). In periodic mode, ProtonProfilerWrapper needs to override shutdown() to also call proton.finalize(). Check gpu_worker.py for existing shutdown/cleanup hooks.

userStories.title: Write tests for contiguous profiling
userStories.description: As a developer, I need tests verifying periodic flushing mode works correctly.
acceptanceCriteria: Unit test: periodic mode uses activate/deactivate instead of start/finalize
Unit test: non-periodic mode continues using start/finalize (no regression)
Unit test: phase number increments on each stop in periodic mode
Unit test: get_status() returns correct phase and file information
Unit test: shutdown calls finalize in periodic mode
Unit test: session is created once and reused across multiple start/stop cycles
All existing profiler tests continue to pass
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Use the _make_wrapper_with_mock() pattern from existing tests. Mock proton.activate, proton.deactivate, proton.data.advance_phase, proton.finalize. Verify call sequences across multiple start/stop cycles.

userStories.title: End-to-end validation of contiguous profiling with vllm serve
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to validate contiguous profiling works end-to-end with the vllm serve command.
acceptanceCriteria: vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b --profiler-config '{"profiler": "proton", "proton_profiler_dir": "/tmp/proton_output", "proton_mode": "periodic_flushing", "proton_hook": "triton"}' starts without errors
First /start_profile + requests + /stop_profile cycle produces .part_0 output file
Second /start_profile + requests + /stop_profile cycle produces .part_1 output file
/profile_status returns correct phase number and file list after each cycle
Output files contain meaningful profiling data (not empty)
userStories.notes: The openai/gpt-oss-20b model requires --tensor-parallel-size 2 on 2x L40S GPUs. Server startup takes ~35-45s. Send chat completion requests between start/stop to generate profiling data.
